skill.name: Objective or subjective language
skill.why: Reports should stick to what anyone can check. Persuaders slip in feelings.
skill.how: Ask: could anyone check this word, or is it someone's feeling or judgement?

steps.say: I'm writing about Bluster Rock. Most of my words anyone can check. One is just my feeling.

show.nudge: Anyone can look and see it's red. Which word is a feeling?
Anyone could measure that. Which word is a feeling?

steps.ask: Tap the word that's only Tully's feeling.
steps.win: Yes! Breathtaking is my feeling. A word that shows a feeling or judgement is subjective.

steps.say: Red and 340 metres are objective. Anyone could check them and get the same answer.

show.nudge: 'Delicious' is Mo's feeling. Could anyone check it?
'Too spicy' is a judgement. Some people love spice.

steps.win: Yes! Anyone can see orange. Delicious and too spicy are Mo's judgements.

steps.say: One feeling word can tip a whole sentence.

show.nudge: You could check the bus was late. Which word adds a feeling?
Anyone could time ten minutes. Which word adds a feeling?

steps.ask: Tap the word that makes it subjective.
steps.win: Yes! Sadly is the writer's feeling. Take it out, and the sentence is objective.

steps.say: Careful! Zed says a number always makes a sentence objective. Check this one.

check.nudge: Anyone could check $50. But could anyone check 'shocking'?

steps.win: Right! A number doesn't make it objective. 'Shocking' is a judgement.

steps.say: And 'I' doesn't make a sentence subjective. Check the other words.
show: I went to the footy on Friday.
steps.ask: What is 'I went to the footy on Friday'?

options.text: objective
subjective, because it says I
options.reason: 'I' just tells you who went. Is there a feeling word?

options.text: subjective, because it's about Tully
options.reason: Is there a feeling word? You could check what day she went.

steps.win: Yes! There's no feeling word, and you could check it. 'I' just tells you who went.

steps.say: Now fix one. Make 'The pool is freezing and horrible' objective.

options.text: The pool is chilly and no fun.
options.reason: 'No fun' is still a judgement. Could anyone check it?

options.text: Sadly, the pool is 18 degrees.
options.reason: The number is fine, but 'sadly' adds a feeling.

options.text: The pool is 18 degrees.

steps.win: Yes! Anyone could measure 18 degrees. No feelings are left.

terms.means: Sticks to what anyone could check, like sizes, colours, dates and prices.
Shows a feeling or judgement, like sadly, breathtaking or too spicy.

card.test: Test each word. Could anyone check it? Objective. A feeling or judgement? Subjective.

encounters.frame: Zed is writing up the comet for the Bluster Rock Science Centre newsletter. It has to read like a science report.
encounters.text: Comet Ferro-2 was first spotted from Bluster Rock on the night of 3 March by Ana Ruiz, a Year 6 student with a home-made telescope. Over the next week, the comet's tail grew to about the width of three full moons across the sky. Astronomers at the science centre tracked it every night and took more than 600 photos. They measured its speed at about 40 kilometres per second. On the clearest nights, people could see the comet without a telescope, low in the western sky just after sunset. The centre opened its roof deck so that visitors could take a look, and about 1,200 people came over the week. The comet faded after eleven nights. Astronomers say it will not return for about 900 years, so none of us will see it again. Ana has been invited to give a talk about her discovery at the science centre next month.

encounters.frame: Ranger Dot gave a talk about dingoes. Wren took notes, but she slipped some of her own feelings in.
encounters.text: Ranger Dot stood on the back of her ute to talk to the crowd. 'Dingoes have lived on Bluster Rock for thousands of years,' she said. 'They can run at up to 60 kilometres an hour, and a pup stays with its family for about a year. They howl to call to their pack, especially at dawn and dusk.' A man in the crowd called out, 'They're far too dangerous to live near towns!' A girl near the front said, 'No way. They're wonderfully clever hunters, and they deserve their space.' Ranger Dot held up a hand. 'There are about 40 dingoes on the island,' she said. 'Their dawn howl is the most beautiful sound in the whole bush. Few visitors ever hear it, because dingoes keep away from people.' Then she handed out a map showing where the dingo dens are, and asked everyone to keep their dogs on a lead.

encounters.frame: Wren is reading the Bluster Bugle's report on the stranded whale. The Thornkit flushed pink at exactly one word.
encounters.text: WHALE RETURNED TO SEA AFTER NINETEEN-HOUR RESCUE. A young humpback whale that became stranded on Red Sand Beach early on Saturday morning was returned to the sea late that night. A fisher spotted the whale at about 5 am and called the island's marine rescue team. It was the first whale stranding on Red Sand Beach since 2015. Volunteers worked in shifts for nineteen hours, keeping the whale's skin wet with buckets and damp sheets while they waited for the tide to rise. Marine scientists estimate that the whale was about eight metres long. Remarkably, the whale was refloated at high tide just before midnight and swam out past the reef. Rescue leader Sione Taufa said the team would watch the bay from a boat for the next two days to make sure the whale did not return to the shallows. The beach was closed to the public until Sunday afternoon. Mr Taufa thanked the 64 volunteers who helped, and asked anyone who sees a stranded animal to call the rescue line rather than trying to move it themselves.
encounters.prompt: The reporter wrote 'Remarkably, the whale was refloated at high tide.' What does 'Remarkably' do to the report?
encounters.success: 'Remarkably' is the reporter's own reaction. It tips one sentence into subjective, so readers get a feeling with the facts.

options.text: It adds the reporter's own surprise, so the report stops being fully objective.
It tells readers exactly when the whale was refloated, so they can check the time.
options.reason: 'At high tide' tells you when. This word adds a feeling instead.

options.text: It makes no difference, because one word can't change a whole sentence.

parts: COME TO THE BLUSTER ROCK PLANETARIUM! Lie back under our brand-new dome and travel to the edge of the solar system without leaving your seat. The planetarium opened in March on the hill behind the Bluster Rock general store.

parts: Shows run at 10 am, 1 pm and 4 pm daily, and bookings can be made at the front desk. Group bookings of ten or more receive a free poster of the planets. The planetarium is wheelchair accessible, and the car park has spaces for forty cars and two buses. Don't miss the experience of a lifetime!

encounters.frame: Two texts describe the old Crowley homestead. One is a museum plaque; the other is a ghost tour flyer.
encounters.text: MUSEUM PLAQUE: The Crowley homestead was built from local sandstone in 1884 by Elsie and Tom Crowley, who ran sheep on the surrounding land for thirty years. The house has six rooms, a cellar and a stone water tank that still holds rain. After the family moved to the coast in 1914, the homestead stood empty until the island council lovingly restored it in 1998. Elsie kept a diary for every year she lived there, and eleven of those charming diaries are now displayed in the front room. Visitors can also see the original iron stove, the shearers' bunks and a rocking chair Tom made from a fallen river red gum. The homestead is open from 10 am to 4 pm on weekends. TOUR FLYER: Dare you enter the Crowley homestead? This eerie ruin has been abandoned for over a century, and its gloomy halls are said to echo with footsteps after dark. The cellar stays below 15 degrees, even on the hottest summer nights. Our expert guides will share the most terrifying tales ever told on Bluster Rock. Some say the ghost of a shearer still searches the house for his lost boots. Tickets are $25, and the tour lasts two hours. Tours depart at 9 pm from the homestead gate. Not suitable for the faint-hearted!
encounters.prompt: Sort these phrases from both texts. Test every word: objective or subjective?
encounters.success: Even the plaque slips in judgements, and the flyer has facts. Judge each phrase, not where it came from.

encounters.frame: Indi is writing an entry for the island's online encyclopedia. Encyclopedia entries must be objective.
encounters.text: THE BLUSTER ROCK BUSH BAND is a folk band formed in 1979 by four sheep shearers who played together in the woolshed after work. The original members were Gwen Pike on fiddle, Reg Pike on accordion, Hamish Doyle on guitar and Lou Tran on the tea-chest bass, a home-made instrument built from a wooden box, a broom handle and a single string. Over forty years, the band has released nine albums and played at more than 2,000 dances, weddings and country shows. In 2006, Reg Pike died suddenly, a week before the band's biggest concert, and his grandson Archie took over the accordion at seventeen. Archie still plays his grandfather's accordion, which has a patch of tape over one of its keys. The band's most requested song is 'Dust on the Woolshed Floor', written by Gwen Pike in 1981 about a shearing competition. In 2019, the island council gave the band an award for forty years of music. Critics have described the band's sound in very different ways. One reviewer called it 'joyful and foot-stomping', while another wrote that it was 'old-fashioned and painfully repetitive'. The band still rehearses every Thursday night in the same woolshed, which now has electric lights and a sign on the door asking visitors to wipe their boots.

encounters.frame: Mo reviewed the movie 'Wombat Warrior 3' for the crew's newsletter. Tully says it is subjective. Mo wants to know why.
encounters.text: WOMBAT WARRIOR 3: A REVIEW BY MO. I watched Wombat Warrior 3 at the Bluster Rock drive-in on Friday night, sitting on the roof of the ute with a bag of lollies. The film runs for three hours and four minutes, which is about two hours longer than it needs to be. It stars a wombat called Digby, who has to stop an evil cockatoo from stealing the island's water supply. The first two films were fun, but this one is tedious, overrated and painfully slow. The jokes are tired, and the big battle scene in the middle is a confusing mess of fur and feathers. The cockatoo gets most of the best lines, while the wombat mostly grunts. The ending sets up a fourth film, which the drive-in owner says will be shown next winter. There is no extra scene after the credits, so you can leave as soon as the music starts. The drive-in charges $12 per car. The only good part is the theme song, which is catchy enough that I hummed it all the way home. Somehow, the film has already made more money than the other two put together. I give it one and a half lollies out of five. Gus loved it, but Gus also likes eating paste.
encounters.prompt: Why is Mo's review subjective rather than objective?
encounters.success: Subjective writing judges. 'Tedious', 'overrated' and 'confusing mess' are Mo's opinions that another viewer, like Gus, could reject.

options.text: It uses judgement words like 'tedious' and 'overrated', which another viewer could disagree with.
It gives numbers like 'three hours and four minutes', which show the writer's view.
options.reason: Anyone could time the film. Numbers like that are the objective parts.

options.text: It uses 'I', as in 'I watched it on Friday', which makes any sentence an opinion.
options.reason: 'I watched it on Friday' uses 'I', but it can be checked. Judgement words make writing subjective.

options.text: It complains about the film, and only complaints like 'painfully slow' count as opinions.
options.reason: Praise is subjective too. 'The theme song is catchy' is a positive opinion.
